subject.title: [Field Report] Chrome 136+ binds CDP to [::1] (IPv6) on Windows — portproxy v4tov4 breaks silently

question: What exact Chromium-backed wording and proof bar should OpenClaw require before adding WSL2/Windows CDP IPv4-vs-IPv6 guidance for this issue?
rationale: A prior PR attempted the right surface but was closed because its universal Chrome 136+ claim was too broad, so automation should not choose the final product wording or proof threshold alone.

options.title: Approve scoped guidance
options.body: Add docs and diagnostic hints for the observed curl/netstat IPv4-vs-IPv6 split while avoiding a universal Chrome-version claim and avoiding a WSL-side `[::1]` auto-probe.

options.title: Require live affected-host proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until a current Windows/WSL2/Chrome setup reproduces the exact `[::1]`-only field signature.

options.title: Decline OpenClaw ownership
options.body: Close the issue as external Windows/Chrome/portproxy behavior and leave only general remote-CDP troubleshooting in OpenClaw docs.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped guidance
recommendation.body: Add docs and diagnostic hints for the observed curl/netstat IPv4-vs-IPv6 split while avoiding a universal Chrome-version claim and avoiding a WSL-side `[::1]` auto-probe.

likelyOwner.reason: This reviewer supplied the current maintainer constraint on the closed attempted fix and is the clearest owner for the proof/writing decision.
